2. Facts relevant are that the predecessor-in-interest of present respondent nos. 1(a)- 1(h) and respondent nos. 2 and 3 as plain-tiffs instituted Partition Suit No.57 of 1994 in thy Court of learned Subordinate Judge, 2na Court Bogra, impleading the petitioners herein alongwith the predecessor of present respondent nos.4(a)-4(f) and respondent nos.5-85 as defendants claiming saham of 1.48 1/6 acres of land out of the suit land measuring 13.35 acres, contending interalia, that the suit jote comprising 13.35 acres of land appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.10 of Mouza Khamarkandi under Police Station-Bogra, District-Bogra, originally belonged to Azim Uddin Mollah, Abdul Mollah and Sabu Mollah in equal share; During ejmali possession said Azim Uddin Mollah and Abdul Mollah transferred their shares to the extent of two third measuring 11 bighas and 17 kathas infavour of Asmat Ullah and Jasmat Ullah both sons of C.S. recorded tenant Azim Uddin Mollah by registered deed dated 09.06.1917 on condition that they would pay vendor's debt . of Tk.450/- to the ex-landlord; Since the sale was a conditional one, the vendors retained possession of the land; The said sale deed was never acted upon for non-payment of the debt to the ex-landlord in compliance with the condition stipulated in the deed; Azim Uddin Mollah died leaving three sons namely Asmat, Jasmat and Najem alongwith two daughters solebi and Sawabi; Sabu Mollah died leaving three sons namely Korban, Muslim and Moyez; Jasmat died leaving full brother Asmat; Said Abdul Mollah died leaving wife Amiron and three sons namely Kashem, defendant no.1 Chand, defendant no.2 Farid and 3 daughters namely Shukimon, defendant no.3 Rupban and Janina; Amiron died leaving two sons Ayetullah and defendant no.2 Farid and daughter defendant no.3 Rupban; Asmat Ullah died leaving two sons namely olam and Nasir and two daughters Toiron and Gendi; Najem died leaving a son plaintiff no.1 Jashim and daughter Lalbibi; Sawabi died leaving a son defendant no,6 Kuranu; Nasir died leaving a son plaintiff no.2 Khairuzzaman Mollah and daughter plaintiff no.3 Shahera; Golan died leaving wife defendant no,7 Kochimon and two daughters namely Jahanara, Jobeda and two sisters Gendi and Toiron; Salebi died leaving two sons Md. Nabir Uddin and Kalim Uddin, defendant nos.10 and 11 respectively; Korban died leaving three sons namely Buhl, Riaz and Kawser; Said Riaz died leaving four sons namely Md. Biraz Uddin, Md. Azizer Rahman, Md. Hafizar Rahman and Md. Abdur Rahman, defen-dant nos.13-16 respectively; Kawser died leaving only daughter defendant no.17 Mosammat Asma and brother Bulu; Moyez died leaving wife Fuljan, a son defendant no. 18 Md. Mojam Uddin and two daughters Most. Kallaton Nesa and Most. Potol Bibi; Fuljan died leaving husband defendant no.10 Md. Nabir Uddin, a son Mojam Uddin and three daughters Kallaton, Potol and Golapi, defendant nos.19-21 respectively; Moslem died leaving a son Samsul and three daughters Borki Bibi, Bull and Momijan, defendant nos. 22-25 respectively; Kashem died leaving a son Futu Mollah, defendant no.26 and three daughters Sonaban Bibi, Fatema Bibi and Rahima Bibi, defendant nos.27-29 respectively; Shukimon died leaving four sons namely Kazem, Sukra, Azo and Kachua alongwith one daughter Atopjan; Said Kazem died leaving defen-dant no.30 Kodban and Atopjan died leaving a daughter defendant no.31 Sharifon and three brothers Sukra, Azo and Kachua; Said Sukra died leaving wife defendant no.32 Hamidon and three sons namely Md. All Fakir, Md. Hachen Fakir and Md. Hamid Fakir alongwith daughter Shurjoban, defendant nos.33-36 respectively; Azo died leaving a son Yousuf Ali and two daughters Momena and Ayjon, defendant nos.37-39 respectively; Jarina died leaving two sons Rabia and Bacha; Said Bacha died leaving wife defendant no. 40 Achiron and brother Rabia; Said Rabia died leaving wife defendant no.41 Maim n, and five sons namely Abul Hossain, Gaffer, Hobibar, Sekander and Nur Hossain and three daughters Asarban, Nurbanu and Asma Khatun, defendant nos.42-49. respectively. Toiron died leaving five sons namely Asgar, Ahab, Dhalu, Bulu and Tutu and two daughters' Jarina and .lamina, defendant nos.50-56 respectively; Gendi died leaving a son defendant no.57 Dilbor and a daughter defendant no.58 Sahera; Kachu died leaving wife Kanchi and two sons Sobhan, Montu alongwith daughter Mariam, defendant nos.59-62 respectively; Defendant nos.1-62 are the co-sharers by inheritance to the suit jote and defendant nos.63-66 are the co-sharers by purchase to the suit jote; The plaintiffs are in ejmali possession; The plaintiffs demanded partition of the suit land from defendant no.26 on 15.06.1992 but he denied; Hence, the suit. 

 5. The case of the defendant nos. 67 and 68 are that the suit jote appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.10 originally belonged to Abdul Azim Mollah, Abdul Mollah and Sabu Mollah; During ejmali possession Azim Mollah and Abdul Mollah transferred their share to the extent of 11 bighas and 17 kathas in the year 1917 to Asmat and Jasmat but the C.S. record was not prepared accordingly; Azim Mollah, Abdul Mollah, Sabu. Mollah, Asmat and Jasmat transferred 22 bighas and 6.75 kathas of land to Shushila Shundari Gbosh, predecessor of the defendants, vide registered deed no.11.2 dated 05.01.1923 prior to the C.S. operation but C.S. record was prepared and published wrongly in the name of Azim Mollah, Abdul Mollah and Sabo Mollah; Though C.S. record was published wrongly but Shushila Sundari Ghosh possessed the purchased land through borgadars; Abdul Pramanik transferred 1.17 acres of land to Rajani Kanta Ghosh, husband of Shushila Sundari vide registered kabala dated 18.12.1928; Both Shushila Sundari and Rajanii. Kanta Ghush gave barga of the suit land infavour of Abdul Pramanik for 7 years by barga deed dated 02.04.1929; Shushila settled .55 acre of land to different persons and the rest to the extent of 10.59 acres was recoraed in the M.R.R. Khatain in her name Rajani Kanta died prior to publication of M.R.R. Khatian; Shushila Sundari died leaving two daughters Radharani and Raj lakshmi, defendant nos.67 and 68 respectively; During the war of liberation Shushila Sundari and her successors engaged Chand Miah son of Abdul Ariz as bargadar in respect of their share and left for India; On their return after liberation when they demanded usufructs from Chand Miah, he denied to give the same and then they filed Title Suit No. 2 of 1974 against Chand Miah which was decreed on compromise in their favour; Rajlakshmi transferred .24 acre of land by registered deed dated 25.06.1989 infavour of defendant no.22 son of defendant no.2; Rajlakshmi also transferred some lands to different persons; After transfer, the defendants retained possession to the extent of 7.43 acres of land; The defendants filed Case No.3713192 under Section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure against defendant no.26 and others which was disposed of in their favour on compromise; Plaintiffs are not entitled to get any saham/relief in the suit and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 11. Mr. Sk. Md. Morshed, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the High Court Division committed an error by not considering that Azim, Abdul, Sabu alongwith Asmat Ullah and Jasmat Ullah executed registered deed dated 05.01.1923 infavour of Shushila Sundari Ghosh, mother of the defendant-appellants, which shows that Asmat Ullah and Jasmat Ullah, purchaser of the land vide registered deed dated 09.06.1917, had been the owner and possessor of the land purchased and which also proves that the registered deed dated 09.06.1917 was duly executed. He also submits that the plaintiffs failed to prove their claim that the debt due to ex-landlord to the extent of Tk.450/- was not paid; He again submits that the document being ancient one clearly establish right, title, interest and possession of the defendant-appellants and their predecessor. He further submits that the defendant-appellants by adducing evidence proved that the respondent-plaintiff's predecessors cultivated the land as bargadar of Shushila Sundari and that the M.R.R. Khatian was prepared duly in the name of defendants' predecessor i.e. Shushila as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set-aside. He also submits that the High Court Division failed to appreciate that the defendant-appellants relayed the land through Advocate Commissioner which is apparent from Advocate Commissioner's report as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set-aside. He lastly submits that the High Court Division wrongly shifted the onus of proof of payment of debt to the ex-landlord by the vendees of kabala dated 09.06.1917 on the defendant-appellants though in view of the kabala dated 05.01.1923 the onus was squarely falls upon the respondent-plaintiffs to prove the non-payment of the dues of ex-landlord by the vendees and as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set-aside. 

 12. On the other hand Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent nos.1(a)- 1(h), 2-3 submits that the deed dated 09.06.1917 executed by Md. Azim Mollah and Md. Abdul Mollah infavour of Asmat Ullah and Jasmat Ullah was a conditional sale and the condition not being complied with, it was not acted upon and accordingly C.S. Khalian was prepared in the name of original owners but the trial court erroneously shifted the onus upon the plaintiffs as such the impugned judgment and decree shall sustain. He also submits that C.S. Khatian has presumption of its correctness which is suit rebatable by proper evidence but no evidence was adduced by the contesting defendants to discharge their onus which lawfully lies on them and the trial court failed to appreciate the evidence adduced by the plaintiffs and thus erroneously holding title and possession of the defendants. He again submits that Khatian has no presumptive value as such the impugned judgment and decree shall sustain and the appeal is liable to be dismissed. He lastly submits that the plaintiffs categorically stated in the plaint that: 

 30. From the aforementioned discussions, we are of the view that since the suit land was purchased by Shushila Sundari before C.S. operation, the C.S. record should have been prepared in her name. Again, on perusal of exhibit-'neo' i.e. M.R.R. khatian no.15 it appears that said khaitian was prepared in the name of Shushila Sundari in continuation of kabala dated 09.06.1917 and 05.01.1923 which are marked as exhibit-la' and ‘kha' respectively, as such said M.R.R khatian was prepared correctly. From the contents of kabala dated 18.06.1080 (exhibit-'pa') and another kabala also dated 18.06.1980 (exhibit-' fa' it appears that defendant no.69 purchased portion of the suit land from the heirs of Shushila Sundari. Thus Trial Court justly arrived at a finding that plaintiffs have failed to prove their title in the suit land.
